name: Dollar Tree, Inc.

profile.description: Dollar Tree is a discount variety retailer headquartered in Chesapeake, Virginia, operating the Dollar Tree banner across the U.S. and Canada after divesting Family Dollar in 2025 (now reported as discontinued operations). Under CEO Mike Creedon, who joined as COO in 2022 and became permanent CEO after an interim stint, it is shifting from a single-price-point model to multi-price assortments and replacing decades-old legacy systems with AI-enabled planning, inventory and workforce platforms. Q2 FY2026 (ended August 1, 2026) total sales grew 7.0% to $4.89B with comparable sales +3.7%; adjusted EPS was $1.39 (+80.5%) and GAAP EPS of $2.70 included a one-time tariff refund. Full-year FY2026 guidance is $20.5-20.7B net sales and adjusted EPS of $7.70-8.05. The company pays no dividend.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Dollar Tree has made a significant strategic shift — exiting Family Dollar (recorded as $4.07B of discontinued-operations losses in FY2024 and $2.26B in FY2023 before the sale) and moving the core banner to multi-price assortments, with Q2 FY2026 comps of +3.7% driven mostly by higher ticket [1][3]. AI Deployment (1/2): Creedon told investors the company is becoming an 'AI-enabled enterprise,' replacing decades-old legacy systems with AI-enabled platforms for assortment planning, inventory visibility and workforce management [2]; no quantified savings have been disclosed. Market Share (1/2): Dollar Tree is the leading fixed-price variety chain, but it is smaller than Dollar General in the dollar-store channel and Q2 traffic contributed little to growth [1]. Product Pipeline (0/2): No named next-generation formats with launch dates and revenue visibility beyond FY2026 guidance of $20.5-20.7B [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D expense is reported [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Dollar Tree's positioning around delivering extreme value and a 'thrill of the hunt' treasure-hunt experience is clear but not a distinctive purpose beyond value retailing [2]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive charitable foundation or quantified community investment was found; the 10-K notes ongoing DOJ reporting obligations from the 2024 resolution of the West Memphis DC 202 investigation [4]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found, and the company went through three CEOs in roughly two years before Creedon was made permanent [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying by executives was identified in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on growth-stock metrics (no dividend). ROE of 46.03% (1.0, 2x weight) and forward P/E of 17.56 (1.0) are at target, revenue growth of 7.0% scores 0.90, and Yahoo's PEG of 1.36 scores 0.82 (2x weight) [5]. D/E of 223.9% (including leases, after large buybacks and the Family Dollar write-downs shrank equity) scores 0.33, and profit margin of 8.04% scores 0.40 [5]. A comparable 5-year revenue CAGR is not available because Family Dollar is restated as discontinued operations only back to FY2022; it is excluded (the FY2022-FY2025 continuing-operations CAGR is ~8.0% from $15.41B to $19.41B, and including it would not change the score) [3]. Weighted sum 6.27 / 8 = 7.84, rounded to 8. Liquidity floor easily cleared at ~$325M average daily dollar volume [5].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Dollar Tree sells low-ticket consumables and variety goods through physical stores where the treasure-hunt experience and sub-$7 price points make e-commerce or AI-driven substitution uneconomic, and no analyst coverage cites AI as a disruption risk; management treats AI as an internal efficiency lever [2]. The residual risk is that AI-optimized pricing and delivery at Walmart and Amazon narrow the value gap over time, keeping it below the immune tier. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue is reported [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: Dollar Tree has made one genuinely hard decision — walking away from Family Dollar after years of losses — and is modernizing its systems, but in Sinek's lens it is still a company defined by price points and turnaround targets rather than a Just Cause. Three CEOs in about two years, a DOJ-supervised compliance program from the DC 202 rodent-infestation case, and growth driven by ticket rather than traffic describe a business recovering its footing, not one playing a long game.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The extreme-value, treasure-hunt positioning describes what the stores sell, not a future state worth sacrificing for; it is interchangeable with other discount retailers and has shifted with the move from $1 to $1.25 to multi-price [1][2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The company cycled through three CEOs in about two years and rebuilt its C-suite [2], and it remains under DOJ-supervised compliance reporting after the DC 202 case [4]. Creedon's call for a 'culture of excellence and accountability' to fix 'inconsistent execution' [2] signals a culture being repaired, not one of established trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found framing Dollar General, Walmart or Five Below as rivals to learn from; the narrative centers on Dollar Tree's own execution and margins [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Divesting Family Dollar and abandoning the single-price-point identity that defined Dollar Tree for decades are real model changes [1][3]. They were driven by losses and inflation rather than a cause, so they score as meaningful adaptation rather than transformative reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership absorbed more than $6B of cumulative discontinued-operations losses in FY2023-FY2024 to exit Family Dollar and refocus on the core banner [3], and is replacing decades-old systems at real cost [2]. The decision came after years of underperformance, so it reads as overdue correction more than a pattern of costly long-term bets.

investment_thesis: Post-Family Dollar, Dollar Tree is a simpler, higher-return business. Q2 FY2026 sales grew 7.0% to $4.89B with comps +3.7% on top of +6.5% last year, adjusted EPS rose 80.5% to $1.39, and management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.70-8.05 on $20.5-20.7B of sales [1]. ROE of 46%, an 8.0% net margin and TTM free cash flow of roughly $9.72 per share (P/FCF ~14x) at 17.6x forward earnings support the case that multi-price assortments and AI-enabled inventory and workforce systems can keep compounding earnings [2][3][5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is earnings quality and leverage. Q2 GAAP EPS of $2.70 was inflated by a one-time tariff refund, FY2026 guidance includes about $0.60 of net tariff-refund benefit, and Q3 adjusted EPS guidance of $0.80-0.95 (including ~$0.50 of refund reinvestment) missed estimates [1]. Growth is coming from ticket rather than traffic, D/E is 224% and price-to-book is 7.7x after Family Dollar write-downs [3][5], and the stock has rallied from a 52-week low of $85.88 to $138.60, near its $142.40 high, leaving little margin for execution slips by a leadership team that is still new [2][5].
key_catalysts: Q3 FY2026 results (early December) confirming comps of 3-4% and net sales of $5.0-5.1B, with progress toward the raised $7.70-8.05 adjusted EPS guide [1]
Margin gains from AI-enabled assortment planning, inventory visibility and workforce-management platforms replacing legacy systems [2]
Further rollout of multi-price assortments lifting average ticket at the core Dollar Tree banner [1]
key_risks: Normalization of earnings once one-time tariff refunds (about $0.60 of FY2026 adjusted EPS) roll off, with Q3 guidance already below consensus [1]
Traffic stagnation — Q2 growth was driven mostly by ticket — as multi-price moves test the brand's value perception [1]
Leverage of 224% D/E and residual compliance obligations from the DOJ DC 202 resolution [4][5]
